items.title: Elon Musk is 'truly a genius,' says Vladimir Putin
items.snippet: Putin said that he and Musk are in "close contact" about Rassvet, Russia's Starlink-like satellite connectivity project.

items.title: As search traffic dries up, Reddit announces it's shifting to a logged-in experience
items.snippet: As AI transforms how people find information online, Reddit is rethinking its open-web roots to protect its audience and business.

items.title: Rivian expands joint venture with VW to include AI assistant
items.snippet: Rivian doesn't disclose if the value of its $5.8 billion joint venture will expand as a result.

items.title: OpenAI-backed Thrive Holdings acquires ADT
items.snippet: OpenAI-backed Thrive Holdings is buying ADT in a $15.3 billion deal, with plans to bring AI to the home security business.

items.title: Where was my invite to the — wait, what? Airbnb had a gala?
items.snippet: Airbnb’s nonprofit held its inaugural gala on Wednesday in Los Angeles, and the internet had one reaction — the *what* gala?

items.title: Meta quietly launches an AI fashion app called Style Sketch
items.snippet: The app connects to Instagram to build a virtual closet from photos you’ve already shared, or lets you add items manually by snapping a photo, recording a quick video, or uploading images from your camera roll.

items.title: Granola crunches up a dictation feature to compete with Wispr
items.snippet: Uno reverse! After Wispr added meeting notes to its dictation app, Granola is adding dictation to its meeting notetaker. The voice AI wars are getting interesting.

items.title: Mistral releases weights for its trillion-parameter AI model, targeting cybersecurity
items.snippet: Mistral says its new model can afford organizations a kind of control over its cyber defenses that closed models can't.

items.title: US investigated Chinese spy plot aimed at Nvidia CEO
items.snippet: A top executive of a Singapore AI cloud company that was accused of illegally selling Nvidia chips to China could also have been a Chinese spy, sources have told the New York Times.

items.title: Ex-Palantir execs launch Dream with $17M from a16z to build AI world models for construction
items.snippet: Dream is grounded in real physics and construction standards. Just as LLMs learn from text, Dream's world model is trained on more than 100 million square feet of building data gathered from permit archives across the United States.

items.title: SuperMe raises $20M for its network of AI expert profiles
items.snippet: SuperMe is a network of AI profiles built from the knowledge of real-life experts. When you ask a question, the platform determines which experts are best suited to answer and creates a group chat with their AI profiles.

items.title: Agent identity startup Mintive lands Cowboy Ventures, Coatue, angels Jeff Dean, Andrej Karpathy
items.snippet: Mintive was founded by two engineers who have been working on AI for decades through Google Brain and Coursera. It's platform promises to help IT easily control enterprise agents.

items.title: Wabi, the AI agent that builds mini apps, now valued at $1.25B after latest round
items.snippet: On Thursday, AI app Wabi, now describing itself as a "personal agent," said it has raised $55 million at a $1.25 billion valuation.

items.title: Bluesky blocks links to leaked DHS employee data as government seeks takedowns
items.snippet: The social networking site is facing criticism for blocking access to the site, which identifies thousands of ICE agents and other employees working for Homeland Security.

items.title: DoorDash to acquire Instacart for $17B
items.snippet: The acquisition would bring two major players in on-demand delivery under one roof, combining DoorDash’s dominance in restaurant takeout with Instacart’s reach in grocery delivery.

items.title: Stop sharing your passwords with AI agents, Bank of America warns customers
items.snippet: The bank’s message follows a trend among financial institutions that are restricting third-party AI agent access.

items.title: Mistral’s Le Chonk is now a top open model for coding, ranking alongside Codex GPT-6.1 Terra
items.snippet: Mistral has released the weights for Large 4, along with some impressive Artificial Analysis scores.

items.title: These Claude Enterprise features let you track AI ROI – what’s new
items.snippet: Is your pricey Claude Enterprise account worth it? Anthropic is trying to surface insights with three tools.

items.title: Opera will run AI locally in your browser now – why that’s a gamechanger and how to try it
items.snippet: Thanks to the newly proposed WebAI web standard, the company will start shipping local AI models with its flagship browser.

items.title: Amazon’s new Echo Studio gives Alexa+ an AI camera to see inside your home
items.snippet: The Echo Studio with Home Camera essentially equips Alexa+ with eyes to enable ‘visual intelligence’ features – but there’s a kill switch.

items.title: iPhone Duo screen cracks: Serious issue or overblown? What we know
items.snippet: Some displays are failing within hours of unboxing. Apple is offering replacements, but is the issue really that widespread?

items.title: Why this new Fitbit feature takes us one step closer to non-invasive glucose tracking
items.snippet: Insulin resistance and blood pressure trends are now available on two new Fitbit devices.

items.title: Windows finally gets a built-in internet speed test tool – how to try it
items.snippet: Available to Windows Insiders, the built-in tool measures your upload and download speeds over Ethernet or Wi-Fi.

items.title: This tool can recover deleted AI chats from your phone – how it works
items.snippet: This new tool proves it’s still best to limit the info you share with chatbots.

items.title: What to Know About China’s Top-Secret Spaceplane

items.title: Old 'Popcorn Time' App Left Hundreds of Thousands of Macs at Risk
items.snippet: If you installed Popcorn Time on a Mac years ago, part of the app may still be running, and it may have left your Mac open to attack. Security firm Eye Research has detailed how Time4Popcorn – an unofficial version of the once-popular movie streaming app – left behind a small update checker that scanned for updates every time the Mac started, even for people who hadn't opened the app in years. The checker basically trusted whatever it downloaded, and gave it full permission to change anything on the Mac. items.title: Apple reveals pricing for Mac Studio with 512GB of RAM
items.snippet: When Apple announced the new M5 Max and M5 Ultra configurations of the Mac Studio in August, it said a configuration with 512GB of RAM would be available in October. Today, the company officially revealed the pricing of that option. If you head to the Mac Studio configurator on Apple’s website, you’ll see the new 512GB upgrade option. As previously announced, the 512GB option is only available with the top-tier M5 Ultra chip that has a 36-core CPU and 80‑core GPU. It’s a $15,500 upgrade over the base configuration of that processor, which has 96GB of unified memory. To put it another way: you’ll pay $22,299 for the Mac Studio with the top-tier M5 Ultra, 512GB of unified memory, and 1TB of storage. You can spec it up all the way to 16TB of storage, which brings the total price to $29,799.00. If you order a Mac Studio with 512GB of RAM, it’ll arrive in late November to early December. items.title: MacBook Pro gets the Dynamic Island but no Face ID, and some fans are irked
items.snippet: The new MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display is the first with a Dynamic Island. The interactive, pill-shaped module is borrowed from the iPhone, but where’s the iPhone’s Face ID? Apple left it out — and some Mac fans are mad. On the iPhone, the Dynamic Island wraps around the TrueDepth camera that powers Face ID. But not on this pricey MacBook Pro — Touch ID still handles login authentication. Instead of the laptop unlocking magically when users look at it, they will need to give it the finger instead. On the new MacBook Pro, which Apple unveiled Wednesday, the Dynamic Island replaces the familiar screen notch with an interactive hub for notifications, music and Siri. And the laptop’s touchscreen — the first ever on a Mac — makes tapping those controls feel more natural than ever. Yet even on a laptop costing thousands of dollars, unlocking the machine still requires Touch ID rather than the effortless glance that Face ID offers on the iPhone. The curious omission exposes a weird gap in Apple’s ecosystem: While the company spent years making its devices feel more seamlessly connecte…

items.title: iOS versions: Explore every iOS version from day one to today

items.title: The touchscreen MacBook Pro completes the circle started 10 years ago
items.snippet: Macworld October 27, 2016 was a day that shook the laptop market. Some of us are still recovering from what Apple did on that day, and how it lead to insanity amongst devoted Mac users. On that day, Apple introduced the first MacBook Pro with the Touch Bar . And the world was never the same. Okay, sarcasm aside, the Touch Bar, on the surface, seemed like a good idea at the time. That idea was to provide more dynamic input capabilities than the standard F keys across the top of the keyboard. items.snippet: Macworld On Wednesday at 1 pm ET, Apple is expected to cap off its Pro and Tell week of announcements with the launch of its first truly new laptop in years and a milestone for the Mac: the first-ever touchscreen MacBook Pro with a new design, a new display, and a new price tag. items.title: Apple Drops App Store Commission by a Whopping 4 Percentage Points in Taiwan
items.snippet: Apple Developer News: Apple is making changes to the Taiwan storefront of the App Store, following discussions with the Taiwan Fair Trade Commission. As of October 31, 2026, the commission rate for standard Apple In-App Purchase and paid app transactions will be 26% on the Taiwan storefront of the App Store on iOS and iPadOS. Currently, that rate is 30%. Well there we go. The App Store in Taiwan — just like in Japan — is fixed. ★

items.title: CISA adds Fragnesia to KEV after PHP2Shell attacks rooted 25 servers

items.title: Cisco patches exploited ASA and FTD zero-day that can crash SSL VPNs
items.snippet: Cisco has released fixes for CVE-2026-76418, a zero-day attackers are exploiting to remotely crash Cisco Secure Firewall ASA and FTD devices. Shadowserver is tracking more than 51,000 Cisco ASA SSL VPN devices exposed online, though that count does not show how many remain vulnerable. Source

items.title: PHP2Shell puts firewall and VPN management interfaces at risk
items.snippet: PHP2Shell’s reach extends beyond websites: embedded PHP can leave firewall, VPN, and other appliance management interfaces exposed to remote code execution. CISA has confirmed active exploitation of the flaws, and added them to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog . Appliance customers often cannot patch PHP themselves; they must wait for vendors to issue updated firmware. Source

items.title: EDK II UEFI flaw leaves PXE-booting servers without a stable fix
items.snippet: A fix for critical EDK II vulnerability CVE-2026-97631 has been merged into the project’s code, but no stable release includes it yet. The flaw can let an attacker run code in firmware while a server boots over the network, before Secure Boot checks startup components. Until hardware vendors ship firmware updates, organizations that do not need PXE boot can disable it to reduce exposure. Source

items.snippet: Welcome to the 26th edition of Cloudflare's DDoS Threat Report. This edition covers the third quarter of 2026 — July, August, and September — and returns the series to its quarterly cadence following the combined H1 2026 volume. The analysis is produced by Cloudforce One, Cloudflare's Threat Intelligence organization, providing a comprehensive analysis of the evolving threat landscape of Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attacks based on data from the Cloudflare network. Across its network in the third quarter of 2026, Cloudflare autonomously mitigated 18.2 million network-layer DDoS attacks and 14.4 trillion HTTP DDoS requests. That works out to approximately 8,226 network-layer DDoS attacks per hour, or about 197,400 per day — one attack every 0.44 seconds. The quarter's mitigated traffic totaled 272.6 PB at the network layer and 95.1 PB at the HTTP layer. items.title: What took the Internet offline in Q3 2026
items.snippet: The Internet can feel invisible when everything is working normally. But when connectivity breaks, the many systems it depends upon become evident in an instant. Because Cloudflare’s global network handles more than 20% of the web’s traffic, it offers a unique perspective of how Internet traffic is behaving. When failures in infrastructure, power, policy, or security disrupt access to the Internet, Cloudflare Radar can observe the impact by monitoring traffic to our customers. Each quarter, we review the disruptions detected and annotated on Radar, highlighting what happened, where it happened, and the broader conditions that shaped each event. In this post, we examine the major categories of Internet disruptions observed during the third quarter of 2026, including government-directed shutdowns, power outages and natural disasters. Between July and September, Internet disruptions were largely driven by failures in the systems the Internet depends on. Power grids failed in Cuba, Honduras, Guam, Ukraine, and several other countries. Natural disasters damaged electricity and telecommun…

items.title: Gartner warns $3.5T in AI infrastructure spending could be at risk by 2030
items.snippet: In another sign that the AI bubble is potentially ready to burst, both Gartner and Elon Musk have predicted a significant consolidation of the neocloud business and revenues to fall very short of expectations in general. Gartner says more than $3.5 trillion in artificial intelligence infrastructure spending could be exposed to asset impairments by the end of 2030 if providers continue investing at their current pace. AI providers are expected to spend nearly $1 trillion on infrastructure in 2026, followed by another $6 trillion in planned investments between 2027 and 2030, according to the report. items.title: Oracle adds Google TPUs to OCI to expand enterprise AI compute options
items.snippet: Oracle has entered into a partnership with Google to bring the latter’s Tensor Processing Units (TPUs) to Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI), giving its enterprise customers an alternative to GPUs for training and inference workloads without running their workloads on Google’s own cloud platform. The deal, which was announced at Oracle AI World in Las Vegas on Tuesday, marks the first time Google TPUs will be available through another hyperscaler, the companies said in a joint statement. As part of the agreement, Oracle will provide the data center infrastructure needed to deploy the TPUs, including power, cooling, and networking, they added. items.title: Cisco’s partner shift: What customers should expect from their Cisco partner in the AI era
items.snippet: Most of the coverage from Cisco Partner Summit will understandably focus on what Cisco is doing for its more than half a million partners. There were new incentives, a revamped deal registration program, and plenty of talk about margins. But I’ve always believed the channel story is really a customer story. When I was a Cisco customer, I relied heavily on my partner for guidance and support. items.title: IBM connects quantum chips with ‘quantum channels’ at 99% accuracy
items.snippet: IBM has reached a critical milestone for scaling quantum computers, the company announced . According to a research paper published last week, superconducting processors have been connected for the first time using multiple quantum channels with an average transfer fidelity of 99%. In addition to trying to get more qubits on a single chip, quantum computers can also be scaled up by linking multiple chips together. In this case, researchers linked two 120-qubit chips with four connectors—that they called l-couplers—each with a superconducting cable 31.5 inches long. items.title: IBM aims to bring AI agent sprawl under enterprise control
items.snippet: IBM is pulling together a package of tools to help enterprises discover, identify, manage, and control the growing number of AI agents in use. items.title: HPE extends AI-driven networking to SD-WAN and SASE
items.snippet: HPE continues to integrate its networking products with its AI-driven Mist platform and Marvis AI engine, this week bringing the HPE Networking EdgeConnect suite—which combines its SD-WAN and SSE products in a unified SASE offering—into the fold. items.title: FluidCloud replaces VDDK with its own disk copy engine for VMware exits
items.snippet: For organizations looking to migrate from VMware, the VMware Virtual Disk Development Kit (VDDK) library is a critical component. VDDK is a set of C libraries for creating and accessing VMware virtual disk files, and until August of this year, it was available as a download. That is no longer the case . Many agentless migration tools used the libraries to read virtual disks. Broadcom has said licensed use of VDDK is for backup and recovery and that it is not a customer entitlement. Organizations partway through a VMware exit are now figuring how they will proceed. It is a gap that FluidCloud is now looking to fill with the vHOP (VM Hopping Engine) service launching today. items.title: Key security concepts NetOps must understand to proactively support SecOps
items.snippet: Network engineers tell me that their security colleagues now routinely provide a list of requests and questions to help them better assess and manage risk. Threat trends and SOC pressures help explain why. Mandiant’s M-Trends 2026 Report finds that adversaries remain undetected on networks longer, often by establishing persistence on edge devices (firewalls, routers, switches and access points) that frequently lack telemetry. Bad actors are also performing more phases of the attack lifecycle from both edge and core network devices.
